page_title: MacClean — Free Mac Cleaner and Disk Space Analyzer

sources.entry: MacClean - Free local Mac disk cleaner that lets you review WeChat media, System Data, and Xcode or AI caches before deleting. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jinglings/MacClean) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: MacClean
summary.one_liner: A free macOS disk cleaner and disk space analyzer that reviews WeChat/QQ/WeCom media, system data, developer caches, app leftovers and duplicate files before anything is removed.
use_cases: Find what is taking up space on a Mac
Clean WeChat, QQ or WeCom photos and videos
Remove Xcode DerivedData and npm, pip or Gradle caches
Find and remove duplicate downloads and documents
Uninstall apps and remove leftover files
Restore recently cleaned files from Cleanup History
summary.what_it_does: MacClean scans a Mac's disk usage and shows folder sizes in Storage Map and a System Data breakdown of snapshots, backups and caches. It lets users review and select WeChat, QQ and WeCom media by type and month, and can group WeChat media by conversation folder with custom labels; it states that message databases are not read. It covers developer caches such as Xcode DerivedData, npm, pip and Gradle, plus local models from Ollama, Hugging Face and LM Studio, with models never preselected. It also finds duplicate and similar files in groups, shows app sizes with related files for uninstalling, and offers browser history, cookie and session clearing while keeping passwords and bookmarks. Ordinary cleanup moves items to the Trash and can be restored from Cleanup History until the Trash is emptied.
notable: Ordinary cleanup goes to the Trash and can be restored from Cleanup History
Source code is public on GitHub under the MacClean Community License
Free for personal and internal business use with all features included and no activation (version 1.6 and later)
Scanning only reads information; files and scan results stay on the Mac
caveats: Selling original or modified copies, or integrating code into a paid product, requires a separate commercial agreement

Not notarized by Apple in the current release, so opening it needs a manual approval step in System Settings; the page also says Trash emptying, Docker cleanup and local snapshot deletion cannot be undone through Cleanup History
